Convert all your rs3 gp to OSRS gp and then restart the grind but BETTER. ~169 hours on steam but over 4k on my main and 3k on each of my two alts. money is of no object to me in RS3 anymore, release of necro bumped my total wealth beyond 15B in just coin not including any unsold loot and sets for Ras. Very enjoyable game, I have over 3 years of logged in playing time over the course of approximately 15 years. This game has taken away many real life opportunities away from me because of it's addictiveness. If your seeking a game with many goals which cannot be completed without a certain amount of RNG or luck mechanism for obtaining in game drops then this is the game for you. Despite the many things to do, they are blocked by RNG. 

Despite that over the years the game has introduced a "Pay to win" mechanism which players can buy XP which is the major downfall of this game, and one of the core reasons the there have been talks about getting loot boxes or loot crates banned as many minors have been buying them without parents permission. Many of the holiday events are very time heavy as well has major updates require time investment and can't be fast forward or skipped. It's got good graphics, ability to have pets, familiars, level up skills, complete achivements, compete with "runescore" against other players. 

The PVP aspect of the wilderness is dead as well as PVP in general, this is a very PVM heavy game, with near end game PVM content involving a degree of elitism to be instilled to get fast times or fast kill times of bosses and monsters. This game is fun and you will meet many players that can be your lifelong friends throughout the journey but in all honesty wouldn't recommend due to what it has taken away from me in real life but at the same time it's just so fascinating to be able to login and chillax with the community so would recommend on that hand.

I've played Runescape way back since 2005, before Runescape 2 and 3. There's always a part of me that yearns to play this game, no matter how old I get. The grind has become immense compared to when I first played, and the micro transactions have kept me from playing any more. Sure, there's an ironman mode you can play to avoid that for the most part, but micro transactions have still become a fundamental feature of the game itself which takes away from the grind many of us suffered in the early days, before you could basically buy experience or items from Jagex themselves.

[h1]Do I recommend this and why?[/h1] 
[b]No![/b] => Even though there's lots of content that's good and there's always new content being added, I find enough about the game off-putting to not play it very much. [h1]“A most refined indulgence… with a touch of obsession.”[/h1]

[b]Recommended[/b]

[hr]

[h2]🎮 First Impressions (A Return to Familiar Lands)[/h2]  
There are few titles that evoke a sense of nostalgia quite like RuneScape.

Whether one arrives as a seasoned veteran or a curious newcomer, the experience begins with a quiet and rather striking realization: this world, in all its simplicity and unassuming presentation, possesses a remarkable and enduring charm.

I first experienced RuneScape long before its arrival on Steam—spending hours upon hours mining rune essence and methodically chopping trees to craft arrows. At the time, it felt routine. In retrospect, it was something far more enduring.

It does not overwhelm. It invites.  
And once accepted, it is exceedingly difficult to abandon.

[hr]

[h2]⚒️ The Pursuit of Mastery[/h2]  
RuneScape is, at its core, an exercise in patience, discipline, and quiet determination.

• Skills are not granted—they are cultivated through effort  
• Progress is gradual, yet deeply satisfying  
• Every milestone feels genuinely earned  

What may initially present itself as repetition soon evolves into something far more compelling: a rhythm. A cadence of effort and reward that transforms routine actions into ritual.

There is, dare one say, a certain elegance to the grind.

[hr]

[h2]🧩 Systems & Progression[/h2]  
The underlying systems of RuneScape are deceptively intricate.

From skill progression to crafting, resource gathering, and long-term goal setting, the game reveals its depth gradually. The absence of rigid direction allows players to define their own pursuits—whether that be mastery of a trade or quiet accumulation of resources over time.

It is a design that rewards both patience and intention.

[hr]

[h2]🌍 A World of Choice and Quiet Immersion[/h2]  
Few virtual worlds offer such unrestrained freedom.

One may spend an evening fishing along a tranquil shoreline, mining in contemplative solitude, or—much like I once did—devoting hours to gathering materials and crafting them into something useful.

There is no imposed urgency, no singular path—only the one you elect to follow.

[hr]

[h2]⚔️ Combat & Challenge[/h2]  
While often understated, RuneScape’s combat offers its own deliberate form of engagement.

Encounters reward preparation, knowledge, and consistency. Success is rarely accidental; it is earned through understanding and execution rather than spectacle.

It is a measured challenge—one that values discipline over haste.

[hr]

[h2]💰 Economy & Player Agency[/h2]  
The economy within RuneScape is not merely functional—it is alive.

Resources gathered, items crafted, and goods traded all contribute to a system shaped by its players. One may find as much success through careful planning and market awareness as through combat prowess.

There is a quiet satisfaction in building something of value through one’s own efforts.

[hr]

[h2]🎵 Atmosphere & Sound[/h2]  
The musical score, while understated, is remarkably effective.

It does not demand attention, but rather enhances the experience with subtlety and consistency. Many pieces linger in memory, not because they overwhelm, but because they accompany the experience so naturally.

[hr]

[h2]👥 Society & Community[/h2]  
The population of RuneScape forms a most intriguing society.

You will encounter the helpful, the industrious, and the relentlessly dedicated—individuals whose commitment to their craft borders on the extraordinary.

It is, in many ways, a shared experience shaped by countless individual journeys.

[hr]

[h2]⚖️ Considerations[/h2]  
• Progress demands a considerable investment of time  
• Certain systems may appear antiquated  
• Newcomers may find the scope overwhelming  

Yet these elements are inseparable from the experience itself—they define it.

[hr]

[h2]🧠 Final Verdict[/h2]  
RuneScape is not a fleeting diversion—it is an enduring pursuit.

It asks for patience, consistency, and a willingness to invest one’s time. In return, it offers something increasingly rare: a sense of progress that feels genuinely earned.

[hr]

[b]Final Thought:[/b]  
One does not simply play RuneScape… one commits to it.

Mtx this and Mtx that. There are certainly some things that seem to have crept up in this game. I can't speak to the f2p aspect of the game as even from the early days of the game I always paid for membership as it just offered SO much bang for your buck and only continues to do so. Is the game perfect? nah? Is the game going to give you that feeling of satisfaction over grinding hours and hours and just watching levels go up as your brain feels good seeing it? yes.

It's kind of fun to know that the game you played as a kid is still alive, but...  Boy howdy, someone left the micro-transaction tap running before leaving the house.  

If you decide to come back, be prepared for an absolute flood of real-world cash grabs, and to be treated like dirt by the company if your only game payment is a monthly subscription to the members' world.

Having been a lifelong player, the "Hero Pass" has been the final nail in the coffin for this MTX machine.

Things to look forward to in Runescape 3:
1. Pop-ups that beg you to spend your money while releasing content at a snail's pace
2. Graphics that are poorer than most Steam Indie games and tick-based combat 
3. One of the highest monthly subscription prices of any MMORPG to date
4. Gambling-style daily keys that do everything short of promise a superb prize if you'd only buy a few more keys
5. A battle pass that will take you approx. 11 hours a day for 3 months in order to obtain the highest level
6. A "premier" membership option that requires a large down-payment for a year - locked in
7. Did I mention the battle pass? Also premier membership? Guess what? It doesn't speed or give you tangible bonuses! You still get to slog for 11 hours daily or spend over $200 dollars to complete the 3-month rotating battle pass!

If you want to experience all new "content" in the form of the slop that Jagex is pushing, it comes at the low low price of around $860 a year - what a steal! Don't forget, you can also buy "bonds" to trade your real world cash for in-game gold so you'll be able to buy inflated degradable items while ruining the game's economy for others! Real winner here.
